title: Teach Cowork a skill
why: A skill is a set of instructions Cowork saves and uses whenever that kind of task comes up, so it does the task your way every time without you explaining it again.
result: A saved skill that does one of your tasks your way, tested in a fresh task.

steps.goal: Choose a task you repeat and let Cowork interview you about how you do it, so your way of working is captured in your own words.
steps.title: Describe the task you want to teach
steps.do: Pick a task you do the same way every time. Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed part, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: I want to create a reusable skill for this task: [a task you repeat, e.g. replying to guest questions about check-in]. Interview me to learn how I like it done: the steps, the format, the tone, and anything to avoid. Ask one question at a time.
steps.see: Cowork asks you questions about the task, one at a time. Answer each one in a sentence or two, because your answers become the skill's rules.
steps.stuck: If it starts doing the task instead, say: "Stop. I want to save this as a skill first." Can't think of a task? Use replying to the messages in guest-messages.txt.

steps.goal: Turn the interview into a saved skill with your rules, an example and a "never" rule, so Cowork can reuse it.
steps.title: Save your answers as a skill
steps.do: When the questions are done, paste this into the same task and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Now save this as a skill called [short name, e.g. guest-reply]. Include my rules, one example of a good result, and at least one thing it should never do.
steps.see: Cowork creates the skill and tells you its name. It may ask you to approve the skill or turn it on. Do that, and note the name.
steps.stuck: If Cowork says it can't save skills in your setup, check Claude's help center at support.claude.com, or ask your Academy program contact.

steps.goal: Check that the skill works without you explaining anything, which shows it is saved and not just remembered in this task.
steps.title: Test the skill in a fresh task
steps.do: Start another new task in your Cowork Academy folder. Ask for the task in your own words, without mentioning the skill, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: [Your request, e.g. Draft a reply to message 3 in guest-messages.txt.]
steps.see: The result follows your format and rules without you explaining them again. That is your skill working.
steps.stuck: If it didn't use the skill, say: "Use my [skill name] skill." Then say: "Update that skill's description so you use it for requests like this one."

steps.goal: Make one change to the saved skill, so you learn how to refine it as you notice what is missing.
steps.title: Improve the skill with one change
steps.do: Improve the skill once. Paste this into the same task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Update my [skill name] skill: [one change, e.g. keep replies under 120 words and always sign off with our team name].
steps.see: Cowork updates the skill, and the next result shows your change. It may ask you to approve the update.
steps.stuck: Be specific. "Keep it under 120 words" works better than "make it better."

atwork: A guest reply skill that always writes in your company's voice
A maintenance summary skill that turns technician notes into owner-friendly updates
A monthly owner update skill that always uses the same structure

title: Save a command you can run any time
why: A command is a saved prompt that runs only when you call it by name, such as open-tickets, so a request you type often becomes one short line. Cowork may save it as a skill, and that's fine: you still run it on demand by name.
result: A saved command you run by name whenever you need it.

steps.goal: Save a request you type often under a short name, so you can run it later with one line.
steps.title: Save a request as a named command
steps.do: Pick a request you type often. Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Save a reusable command called [short name, e.g. open-tickets]. When I run it, it should [the request, e.g. read maintenance-tickets.csv in this folder and list every ticket with status Open, grouped by property]. Only run it when I call it by name.
steps.see: Cowork creates the command, possibly as a skill, and tells you its name. It may ask you to approve it or turn it on. Do that, and note the name.
steps.stuck: If Cowork says it can't save commands or skills in your setup, check Claude's help center at support.claude.com, or ask your Academy program contact.

steps.goal: Run the saved command in a fresh task to prove it works without you retyping the request.
steps.title: Run the command in a new task
steps.do: Start another new task in your Cowork Academy folder. Type / to see if your command appears in the list, or paste this and press Enter.
steps.see: Cowork does the saved request without you explaining it again, for example a list of open tickets grouped by property. Notice that you only typed the command name.
steps.stuck: Nothing in the / list? That's fine. Asking for it by name works the same way.

steps.goal: Change the command so it asks for the detail it needs each time, which makes one command useful in more situations.
steps.title: Make the command ask a question first
steps.do: Make it ask for what it needs first. Paste this into the same task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Change my [command name] command so it first asks me [what it needs, e.g. which property to focus on] before it starts.
steps.see: The next time you run it, Cowork asks your question first, then does the task. Notice that your answer changes the result.
steps.stuck: To see exactly what it does, say: "Show me the instructions saved in my [command name] command."

atwork: weekly-recap: turns your week's notes into a status update for your manager
owner-prep: builds a one-page brief before an owner call
turnovers: lists this week's check-outs that need cleaning, by property

title: Connect an app and use your real data
why: Connectors let Cowork work with the apps you already use, such as email, calendar and shared files. Only connect apps your company has approved, always with your work account, and tell Cowork not to send, change or delete anything.
result: Cowork turning information from an approved work app, or the practice inbox, into a sorted list with draft replies.

steps.goal: Decide which source to use before connecting anything, so you only link an app your company has approved.
steps.title: Choose which approved app to use
steps.do: Choose one app your company has approved for Claude, such as your work email or calendar. If no app is approved yet, skip this step and use guest-messages.txt, which is already in your Cowork Academy folder.
steps.see: You know which approved app you'll use, or you're practicing with guest-messages.txt. Either is fine.
steps.stuck: Not sure what's approved? Ask your manager or your Academy program contact before you connect anything.

steps.goal: Give Cowork read access to your chosen app, by signing in yourself, so it can work with your real information.
steps.title: Connect the app in connector settings
steps.do: Connect the app in Claude's connector settings. A sign-in pop-up appears: sign in yourself with your work account.
steps.see: The app shows as connected. If it doesn't, check you finished the sign-in pop-up.
steps.stuck: Pop-up blocked? Allow pop-ups and try again. Can't find the connector settings, or the app isn't listed? Check Claude's help center at support.claude.com, or ask your Academy program contact.

steps.goal: Ask Cowork to fetch the real information from your app, so you work from actual data and not made-up examples.
steps.title: Pull real information into Cowork
steps.do: Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Using my [app, e.g. work email] connector, or guest-messages.txt in this folder if I'm practicing, show me [what you want, e.g. guest messages from the last 3 days]. Don't send, change or delete anything.
steps.see: Real information from your app, or the 8 practice messages, listed in Cowork. Notice that these are your items, not made-up examples.
steps.stuck: If Cowork says it can't reach the app, reconnect it in Claude's connector settings and try again, or use guest-messages.txt for now.

steps.goal: Turn the raw list into something you can act on, with the most urgent items first and drafts ready for your review.
steps.title: Sort it and draft replies
steps.do: Paste this into the same task, change the bracketed part, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Turn that into [something useful, e.g. a list sorted by urgency, with a draft reply for the two most urgent]. Keep any replies as drafts. I'll review and send them myself.
steps.see: A useful result built from the data. With the practice inbox, the locked-out guests and the Driftwood AC problem should be near the top. Notice that replies are drafts, not sent.
steps.stuck: If Cowork offers to send anything, say no. Cowork drafts, and you send.

atwork: Each morning: guest emails sorted by urgency, with draft replies to review
Each Monday: this week's arrivals and owner calls from your calendar
A shared drive checked for house rules or rate sheets that are out of date

title: Create a report from your data
why: Most reports are copy, paste, chart and explain, over and over. Cowork can do the analysis and the write-up, so you check and decide.
result: A Word report with findings, charts and recommendations from bookings.csv, plus a skill to repeat it next month.

steps.goal: Have Cowork read the booking data and tell you what matters most, so the report has something worth saying.
steps.title: Find the top three findings
steps.do: bookings.csv is already in your Cowork Academy folder. Paste this into your Cowork task and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Open bookings.csv in this folder. Tell me the 3 most important findings about revenue, channels and cancellations, anything unusual, and what I should do about it. Show the numbers behind each one.
steps.see: Three findings in plain English with real figures, such as revenue by channel or which channel has the most cancellations. Notice any surprise it flags as unusual.
steps.stuck: If Cowork says it can't find the file, check that bookings.csv is in the folder this task is using. Missing it? Use the download link below.

steps.goal: Package the findings into a document you can share, with a summary, charts and recommendations.
steps.title: Turn the findings into a Word report
steps.do: Paste this into the same task and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Turn this into a 1 to 2 page Word report saved in this folder as bookings-report.docx: a summary at the top, 2 charts, the findings, and 3 recommendations. Put the charts inside the document.
steps.see: bookings-report.docx appears in your Cowork Academy folder. Open it and check that the summary, charts and recommendations are there.
steps.stuck: Charts missing from the file? Say: "Put the charts inside the document itself." Want a PDF too? Say: "Save a PDF copy as well."

steps.goal: Check one figure yourself before the report goes anywhere, because a wrong number damages trust in the whole report.
steps.title: Check one number before sharing
steps.do: Check one number before you share anything. Paste this into the same task and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Show me how you calculated the first finding, step by step, so I can check it.
steps.see: The calculation broken down so you can follow it, with totals you could check in the spreadsheet yourself. Confirm at least one total.
steps.stuck: If a number looks wrong, say which one and ask Cowork to recalculate it and update the report.

steps.goal: Save the process so next month you give Cowork a new export and get the same report in one step.
steps.title: Save the report as a repeatable skill
steps.do: Make it repeatable. Paste this into the same task, change the bracketed part, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Save this as a skill called [name, e.g. monthly-bookings-report] so next month I can give you a new bookings export and get the same report in one step.
steps.see: Cowork creates the skill and tells you its name. It may ask you to approve it or turn it on. Note the name for next month.
steps.stuck: If Cowork says it can't save skills in your setup, check Claude's help center at support.claude.com, or ask your Academy program contact. To run it every month, pair it with the "Schedule a task" guide.

atwork: A monthly revenue report by property from your booking system export
A weekly bookings and cancellations summary by channel for leadership
Guest review themes by property, ready for the operations meeting

title: Build an interactive tool (an artifact)
why: Cowork can build small interactive pages, such as a calculator, a checklist or a dashboard, and save them as HTML files in your folder. You open the file in your browser whenever you need it, and share it by sending the file or putting it on a shared drive.
result: A working interactive tool saved as an HTML file in your Cowork Academy folder, built without writing code.

steps.goal: Tell Cowork what tool you need in plain words, and it builds a working version for you without any code.
steps.title: Describe the tool you want built
steps.do: Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Build a simple interactive [tool, e.g. stay cost calculator with nightly rate, nights and cleaning fee] for my work as a [role, e.g. reservations agent]. Save it in this folder as [name, e.g. stay-calculator].html so I can open it in my browser.
steps.see: A new HTML file with the name you chose appears in your Cowork Academy folder. Cowork may also show a preview.
steps.stuck: Not sure what to build? Try a turnover checklist for cleaners, or a calculator for a guest's total stay cost.

steps.goal: Use the tool with real values to see that it works the way you expected, before you change anything.
steps.title: Open the tool and try it out
steps.do: Open the HTML file from your Cowork Academy folder. It opens in your web browser. Click around and enter some real values.
steps.see: The tool responds as you use it: totals update and items check off. Notice anything that behaves differently from what you wanted.
steps.stuck: Something doesn't work? Go back to your Cowork task, describe what you clicked and what happened, and ask Cowork to fix the file.

steps.goal: Ask for one improvement and your company colors, so the tool fits how you really work.
steps.title: Add a feature and your colors
steps.do: Make it yours. Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed parts, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Update [name].html: add [one feature, e.g. a discount for stays of 7 nights or more] and use our company colors ([colors, e.g. navy and sand]). Save it over the same file.
steps.see: Refresh the page in your browser and your changes appear. Notice that the new feature and colors are both there.
steps.stuck: Ask for one change at a time. It's quicker to steer.

steps.goal: Confirm the tool is a saved file that works any time, which also tells you how to share it.
steps.title: Reopen it to confirm it is kept
steps.do: Close the browser tab. Open the HTML file from your Cowork Academy folder again.
steps.see: The tool is still there and still works. To share it, send the file or put it on a shared drive.
steps.stuck: Can't find the file? Look in your Cowork Academy folder in Documents, or say in your Cowork task: "Tell me the exact name of the HTML file you saved."

atwork: A stay cost calculator the reservations team uses on calls
An occupancy dashboard you refresh by asking Cowork to rebuild it from the newest bookings export
A turnover checklist that new cleaners tick through at each property

title: Schedule a task to run by itself
why: A scheduled task is Cowork doing work on a timetable, such as a daily brief or a weekly summary, without you asking each time. Scheduled tasks may only run while your computer is on and the Claude app is open.
result: A task that runs on a schedule and saves its result for you to review.

steps.goal: Put the job in one sentence first, so the schedule you set up in the next step has a clear purpose.
steps.title: Write down what you want automated
steps.do: Finish this sentence for your job: "Every [when], I want [what] so I can [why]."
steps.see: You have one sentence that describes your task: when, what and why. Keep it handy for the next step.
steps.stuck: Example: "Every Monday at 8am, I want a list of open maintenance tickets from maintenance-tickets.csv, grouped by property, so I can plan the week."

steps.goal: Turn your sentence into a task that runs on its own at the time you choose.
steps.title: Create the scheduled task
steps.do: Paste this into your Cowork task, change the bracketed parts to match your sentence, and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Create a scheduled task: every [day and time, e.g. Monday at 8am], [what to do, e.g. read maintenance-tickets.csv in this folder and list the open tickets by property]. Save the result in this folder. Show me a sample of what it will produce.
steps.see: Cowork confirms the day and time of the schedule and shows you a sample of the result. Notice that the time matches your sentence.
steps.stuck: If scheduling isn't available in your setup, check Claude's help center at support.claude.com, or ask your Academy program contact.

steps.goal: Test the schedule now instead of waiting, so you see the output before it runs unattended.
steps.title: Run it once now to check
steps.do: Paste this into the same task and press Enter.
steps.prompt: Run that scheduled task once now so I can check the result.
steps.see: The same kind of result you'll get every time it runs, saved in your Cowork Academy folder. Open the file and check it is what you wanted.
steps.stuck: Not quite right? Say what to change, then run it again.

steps.goal: Confirm the task is registered and see when it will next run.
steps.title: See your scheduled tasks
steps.do: Paste this into the same task and press Enter.
steps.see: Your task is listed with its next run time. Keep your computer on and the Claude app open at that time.
steps.stuck: If it didn't run when expected, check that your computer was on and the Claude app was open. Safety habit: have scheduled tasks draft emails, not send them. You press send.

atwork: A daily 8am brief of today's check-ins, check-outs and urgent guest messages
A weekly list of open maintenance tickets for the operations meeting
A monthly reminder of owner contracts coming up for renewal
